name: CodeCrafters
price_of_comparable_item: No dollar amount on the public pricing page (checked 2026-10-28). TechCrunch, 19 Nov 2024: $120 for 3 months, $360 for a year, $990 lifetime. Those figures were not on the page checked today.
what_it_sells: Graded challenges to rebuild Redis, SQLite, Git, Kafka, and others. You work in your own editor and git push to run tests. Instructions are free to read; tests run on the first two stages without a membership, and on every stage of a challenge marked free.
positioning_line: The hardest programming challenges on the internet.

name: KodeKloud
location_or_channel: online; company address on the pricing page is Singapore
price_of_comparable_item: The live pricing page did not render a number (checked 2026-10-28). Capterra's pricing page lists Standard at $15 per user per month, Pro at $30, AI at $46, and Business at $330 per user per year. KodeKloud's own legacy pricing page still shows Standard at USD 15/month paid yearly ($180) or USD 35/month, and Pro at USD 30/month paid yearly ($360) or USD 70/month.
what_it_sells: Video courses plus browser labs for DevOps
source_date: and cloud certifications. The homepage says 1
column12: 000+ enrolled and offers a free start with no credit card.

name: iximiuz Labs
price_of_comparable_item: Free: one playground and one hour a day. Tinkerer playgrounds: $6/month billed as $72/year. Complete Bundle: $10/month billed as $120/year, or $360 once. 30-day money-back guarantee on Tinkerer.
what_it_sells: Real Linux virtual machines in the browser (SSH or browser), plus tutorials, skill paths, and 150+ challenges on the paid bundle. Free tier is smaller VMs with no persistence.
positioning_line: Learn by doing, not just by reading or watching

name: SadServers
price_of_comparable_item: Hobbyist: free. Pro: $9/month or $72/year. Pro+: $11/month, $88/year, or $249 once. Business: $245/month or $1,470/year. A pay-per-use business option starts at $400.
what_it_sells: Browser labs that break a Linux or DevOps setup and ask you to fix it. Pro is unlimited practice on 125+ scenarios. Business plans are for recruiting and training.
positioning_line: Real Challenges. Real Infra. Real Skills.

name: Killercoda
price_of_comparable_item: Free for every scenario except the paid courses. The pricing page lists PLUS and COURSE memberships and did not show a price (checked 2026-10-28). Free sessions last one hour; a paid membership raises that to four.
what_it_sells: Browser scenarios for Kubernetes, Docker, Linux, and related tools, including community scenarios. COURSE adds CKA, CKAD, and CNPE scenario courses.

name: Boot.dev
location_or_channel: online; the pricing FAQ says the company is based in the United States
price_of_comparable_item: Pricing page on 2026-10-28: $399/year, shown as $33/month billed yearly, with a 30-day refund. Their own article, checked by them in August 2026, also states $59/month or $399/year. Purchasing-power discounts exist; an India price was not on the USD page.
what_it_sells: A membership for interactive backend courses (Python, Go, SQL, Docker, and computer science), with quizzes, solutions, and an AI tutor behind the paywall. Lesson text stays readable without paying.
positioning_line: We are a self-paced, gamified online learning platform for learning back-end web development and computer science.

name: Scaler Academy
price_of_comparable_item: Scaler's own fee article, updated 8 Dec 2025, lists Scaler Academy at ₹3.64 lakh to ₹3.99 lakh. The academy page shows ₹9,791/month with ₹20,000 upfront. Scholarship language on the site goes up to ₹25,000.
what_it_sells: A 10- to 12-month live programme in software and AI engineering: programming
column12: Software Engineering hasn't changed. What it takes to be great at it, has.

name: ByteByteGo
price_of_comparable_item: The pricing page fetched on 2026-10-28 lists the courses and the line Pay Once, Own Forever, and does not show a price.
what_it_sells: Written interview-prep courses: system design, coding patterns, object-oriented design, machine learning system design, and related tracks.
positioning_line: Your Interview Prep, All in One Place

name: MIT 6.5840
price_of_comparable_item: No purchase price. The Spring 2026 schedule, lecture list, and paper questions are public. Taking it for credit means enrolling at MIT.
what_it_sells: A graduate distributed-systems subject. Spring 2026 labs on the public schedule: MapReduce, a key/value server, Raft, KV Raft, and a sharded key/value store. Assigned readings include MapReduce, GFS, and Raft.
positioning_line: It will present abstractions and implementation techniques for engineering distributed systems.

name: Mini-LSM
price_of_comparable_item: Free. The course page says everything public now will remain free. Code is Apache 2.0. The book is CC BY-NC-SA 4.0.
what_it_sells: A three-week course to build an LSM-tree storage engine in Rust, including compaction, crash recovery, MVCC, and transactions. It does not include SQL or Raft. You run it on your own machine. Tests are included and the page says they are not exhaustive.
positioning_line: Mini-LSM is a hands-on course for systems and backend engineers.

name: PingCAP Talent Plan
price_of_comparable_item: Free on GitHub. No price is published.
what_it_sells: Open-source courses. The distributed-systems series implements Raft and a key/value service, adapted from MIT 6.824, plus TinyKV and TinySQL.
positioning_line: Talent Plan is an open source training program initiated by PingCAP.

name: CMU 15-445 public projects
price_of_comparable_item: No purchase price on the public project page. Enrollment is a CMU course. This pass used the Fall 2024 project page; a later term's page was not fetched.
what_it_sells: Public BusTub projects. The Fall 2024 query-execution page says Project 1 is a buffer pool and Project 2 is a B+ tree index, then query operators.
positioning_line: At this point in the semester, you have implemented many internal components of a database management system.
